title: Tom Cruise's Jack Reacher Sequel Turns Ten
excerpt:
A decade after Never Go Back, Tom Cruise's unlikely casting remains a talking point.
The films and Alan Ritchson's series offer distinct interpretations of Lee Child's hero.
body_md:
Tom Cruise faced skepticism when he first played Lee Child's towering former military investigator in the 2012 film Jack Reacher. The literary hero is described as exceptionally tall and powerfully built, making Cruise an unconventional physical match. Nevertheless, the first film connected with moviegoers and earned roughly $218 million worldwide.

Its sequel, Jack Reacher: Never Go Back, arrived on October 21, 2016, with Edward Zwick directing. Cobie Smulders played Major Susan Turner, whose espionage accusation pulls Reacher into a conspiracy. The follow-up grossed approximately $162 million worldwide, less than its predecessor, and drew a more mixed reception.

A tenth-anniversary retrospective contrasts Cruise's quick-thinking, agile screen presence with Alan Ritchson's imposing portrayal in Prime Video's Reacher. Ritchson more closely resembles the novels' physical description, but the article argues that both interpretations have their own appeal. It is a retrospective opinion rather than an announcement of another film.
